title: Free characteristic criterion for relative normal crossings over an arbitrary field
statement: Let $F$ be a field [def-weil-field], $X$ a finite-type $F$-scheme [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $B\subseteq X$ a closed subset with dense open complement $j:U\hookrightarrow X$. Let $M=\mathcal O_X\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$ on the small etale site be its divisorial log structure [def-trf-log-regular-pair]. The following conditions are equivalent. (a) The triviality locus of $M$ is exactly $U$, $M$ is fine saturated [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], $(X,M)\to(\operatorname{Spec}F,F^\times)$ is log smooth [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale], and at every geometric point $\bar x$ the characteristic monoid $\overline M_{\bar x}$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf N^{r(\bar x)}$ for some finite $r(\bar x)\geq0$. (b) Etale locally at every geometric point there are a neighbourhood $V\to X$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], an integer $r\geq0$, and a smooth $F$-morphism $c:V\to\mathbf A^r_F$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-affine-space] such that the reduced closed subscheme with support $B\times_XV$ is exactly $c^{-1}V(z_1\cdots z_r)$, and $\mathbf N^r\to\mathcal O_V$, $e_i\mapsto c^*z_i$, is a chart for $M|_V$. The neighbourhood can be chosen so that all $r$ coordinate boundary branches pass through the chosen point. Either condition implies that $(X,B)$ is log regular, $X$ is smooth over $F$, and every intersection of any subset of the local coordinate branches is smooth over $F$ of the expected codimension. Conversely, if $X/F$ is smooth and the reduced closed subscheme with support $B$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor], then (a) and (b) hold. No perfection hypothesis on $F$ is imposed; $B=\varnothing$ and $r=0$ are allowed. This criterion asserts local normal crossings, allowing self-intersections of global components.

source.place: VI 1.4--1.8, pp.69--70; X Proposition 1.2 with the trivial group and trivial base log structure, pp.136--139, and X Lemma 2.2 proof p.149, smooth-pair-over-a-field remark. The sharp free chart specialization gives the relative version of VIII 3.4.4; VIII Remark 4.2.2(i), p.118, is the strict intersection criterion. No Stacks tag states the logarithmic equivalence.

proof.text: All constructions are local near the chosen geometric point. The finite-type hypothesis makes $X$ Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since a field is Noetherian. Assume (a). The trivial log field is log regular: its log ideal is zero, its local ring is a field and its characteristic has rank zero. Apply [lem-sfb-log-smooth-preserves-log-regularity] to obtain log regularity of $(X,M)$. Now [lem-trf-log-regular-sharp-chart] gives an affine pointed etale neighbourhood $V$ and a chart by $P=\overline M_{\bar x}\simeq\mathbf N^r$ inducing the specified characteristic at $\bar x$. Write $t_i$ for the images of its basis. Each $t_i$ is a nonunit at $\bar x$, so each branch contains that point. The chart gives the $F$-morphism $c=(t_1,\ldots,t_r):V\to\mathbf A^r_F$. Log smoothness remains valid on $V$ by the strict-etale locality of [lem-sfb-log-smooth-composition-strict-base-change].

source.place: VI 1.8 and 1.6, printed p.70: log regularity first, then sharp chart; X 1.2 proof, pp.136--138, free-chart specialization

proof.text: Give $T=\mathbf A^r_F$ the associated log structure of $\mathbf N^r\to F[z_1,\ldots,z_r]$, $e_i\mapsto z_i$, using [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. Its structural map to the trivial log field is log smooth by [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale]: the chart is $0\to\mathbf N^r$, its group map has zero kernel and torsion-free cokernel, and its comparison is the identity. The source chart identifies $M|_V$ with the pullback of this log structure, so $c$ is strict. From [def-per-log-differential-stalk] the polynomial logarithmic differential module is free on $d\log z_i$: the relations give $dz_i=z_i d\log z_i$, and an inverse sends $d\log z_i$ to $e_i$ and $df$ to $\sum_i z_i(\partial f/\partial z_i)e_i$. For a unit $u$ its logarithmic image must be $u^{-1}du$. The same calculation holds on etale neighbourhoods: [lem-weil-pbc-flat-unramified-formally-etale] gives a unique lift across the square-zero algebra $B\oplus B^r$ of the identity of any etale algebra $B$, with polynomial structure $f\mapsto(f,\sum_i z_i\partial_i f\,e_i)$. Its second component is the unique extending derivation. These extensions commute with etale restrictions by uniqueness, and passing to the geometric-stalk colimit gives the inverse there too. Thus the logarithmic differential fibre of $T/F$ at every geometric point is freely generated by the $d\log z_i$.

source.place: X proof of Proposition 1.2, p.138, computation of the logarithmic differential module of the chart target

proof.text: Put $k=\kappa(\bar x)$. Apply [lem-sfb-log-cotangent-characteristic-quotient] to $V$ over the trivial log field. Its surjection $k\otimes\omega_{V/F}\twoheadrightarrow k\otimes_{\mathbf Z}\overline M_{\bar x}^{\rm gp}=k^r$ sends $d\log t_i$ to the $i$th basis vector. Hence the map from the logarithmic differential fibre of $T/F$ to that of $V/F$ is injective: a relation among its basis images maps to the same relation among the basis vectors of $k^r$. Both log schemes are log smooth over the same base, and $c$ is strict. Thus [lem-sfb-strict-log-jacobian-criterion] makes $c$ smooth on a neighbourhood of $\bar x$. Shrink $V$ to this neighbourhood. No separability or perfection assumption on $F$ was used.

source.place: X proof of Proposition 1.2, pp.136--138, map (1) and strict Jacobian argument

proof.text: Record the geometry of any smooth comparison $c:V\to\mathbf A^r_F$. For $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,r\}$, put $T_J=V(z_i:i\in J)$ and $V_J=V(t_i:i\in J)$. Then $T_J\simeq\mathbf A^{r-|J|}_F$ and $V_J=V\times_TT_J$ scheme-theoretically. Work locally where $c$ has constant relative dimension $d$, using [sbc-lem-smooth-relative-dimension-locally-constant]. By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], $V_J\to T_J$ is smooth of relative dimension $d$, $V_J/F$ is smooth of relative dimension $d+r-|J|$, and $V/F$ is smooth of relative dimension $d+r$. To verify pure codimension, work on a finite-type affine neighbourhood of a generic point $\eta$ of an irreducible component of $V_J$. The local ring of $V_J$ at $\eta$ has dimension zero. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-at-point-local-ring-trdeg] to this affine intersection and to the ambient affine neighbourhood at the same point: the residue fields agree, so subtraction gives $\dim\mathcal O_{V,\eta}=|J|$. This is exactly the height of the prime of that component in the ambient affine ring. Consequently every nonempty $V_J$ is smooth of the expected pure codimension $|J|$.

source.place: Tag 00P1, lemma-dimension-at-a-point-finite-type-field, applied at a generic point of the intersection; smooth dimension permanence: morphisms.tex Tags 01VA, 01VB and 02G1. This dimension calculation replaces the need for flat pullback of regular immersions (067P).

proof.text: The scheme $V$ and all the $V_J$ of Step 4 are regular by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular]. At a point $v$, discard the $t_i$ which are units in $R=\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Each remaining quotient $R/(t_i)$ is a regular local ring, hence a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]; thus $(t_i)$ is prime. Two of these prime ideals cannot be equal: their common zero scheme would then have codimension one, whereas Step 4 gives codimension two for their intersection. Consequently the nonunit $t_i$ are pairwise nonassociated prime elements in the domain $R$. If a power of $f$ is divisible by $\prod t_i$, primality makes every $t_i$ divide $f$; successive cancellation and pairwise nonassociation make their product divide $f$. Therefore $(\prod t_i)$ is radical. Its zero scheme is reduced, including the empty product case, and has support the union of the coordinate branches.

source.place: Tag 056S, lemma-smooth-regular; algebra.tex Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain; elementary prime-element argument for the product ideal

proof.text: In a chart by $\mathbf N^r$, the characteristic at any point is obtained by discarding exactly the basis elements whose images are units: if a monomial is a unit in a local ring then each of its factors is a unit. Thus it is $\mathbf N^s$ for the number $s$ of vanishing coordinates, and the triviality locus is $D(t_1\cdots t_r)$. Under (a) this locus is $U\times_XV$ by the added triviality-locus requirement. Step 5 now identifies the reduced closed subscheme on $B\times_XV$ with $V(t_1\cdots t_r)$, proving (b). Conversely, given (b), the chart makes $M$ fs, gives precisely these free characteristic monoids, and has triviality locus $U$. The compatible charts $0\to\mathbf N^r$ have zero kernel and torsion-free group cokernel; their comparison is exactly the assumed smooth $c$. Hence [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale] gives (a). Its etale-local formulation applies on the covering neighbourhoods. All coordinates in the (a)-to-(b) construction vanish at the distinguished point by Step 1.

source.place: VI 1.1--1.4, pp.69--70; X Proposition 1.2, pp.136--138, chart interpretation

proof.text: The trivial log field is log regular: its nonunit log ideal is zero, its local ring is a field of dimension zero, and its characteristic has rank zero. On the charts just proved, $0\to\mathbf N^r$ has injective group map and torsion-free cokernel. Apply [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] to these charts to obtain log regularity of $(X,M)$; its recovered divisorial structure and its triviality locus agree with the specified pair by Step 6. Also $V/F$ is smooth by Step 4, so smoothness descends along the etale covering $V\to X$ by [lem-trf-etale-source-smoothness]. Step 4 already proves the asserted smoothness and expected codimensions for all local branch intersections. Thus either condition gives all the stated consequences.

source.place: VI 1.4 and 1.8, pp.69--70; smoothness descent: Stacks descent.tex Tag 036U, lemma-smooth-smooth-local-source

proof.text: For the final converse, suppose $X/F$ is smooth and $D=B_{\rm red}$ is a relative strict normal crossings divisor as defined in [def-trf-smooth-strict-normal-crossings-divisor]. Fix $x$. Delete the finitely many components not containing $x$; call the remaining ones $C_1,\ldots,C_r$. Each $C_i$ is smooth of codimension one, and $Z=\bigcap_i C_i$ is smooth of pure codimension $r$. Apply [lem-pur-smooth-pair-local-coordinates] separately to $C_i\hookrightarrow X$ to obtain a local generator $t_i$ of its ideal. In its coordinate chart the regular sequence has length one: at a generic point of $C_i$ the ambient local ring has dimension one and the quotient dimension zero, so [lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula] forces this length to be one. Shrink to a common affine neighbourhood, with $I_Z=(t_1,\ldots,t_r)$. Apply the same smooth-pair coordinate lemma to $Z\hookrightarrow X$: its ideal is locally generated by a coordinate regular sequence of some fixed length $b$. At a generic point of a component of $Z$ meeting this neighbourhood, the ambient local dimension is $r$ by pure codimension and the quotient local dimension is zero. Again [lem-trf-regular-sequence-dimension-formula] gives $b=r$. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-conormal-free] gives a locally free conormal module of rank $r$ on this neighbourhood of $x$. The specified $r$ generators $t_i$ therefore form a basis of its fibre $(I/I^2)\otimes\kappa(x)$, where $I=I_{Z,x}\subset\mathcal O_{X,x}$.

source.place: Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure, including its regular-sequence assertion; codimension from regular-sequence dimension drop, Mathlib/RingTheory/KrullDimension/Regular.lean, ringKrullDim_add_length_eq_ringKrullDim_of_isRegular, lines 210--214; algebra.tex Tag 00LN, lemma-regular-quasi-regular, for the conormal basis.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-conormal-sequence-smooth-immersion] to $Z\hookrightarrow X$ over $F$; its hypothesis is the smoothness of $Z/F$, not perfection of $F$. Its injective first arrow sends the conormal basis from Step 8 to $dt_1,\ldots,dt_r$. Thus these differentials are independent in $\Omega_{X/F,x}\otimes\kappa(x)$. On the affine finite-type neighbourhood the differentials of finitely many algebra generators span this vector space, by the defining Leibniz relations. Extend the independent $dt_i$ to a basis by selecting differentials $dg_1,\ldots,dg_s$ from that spanning family. Now [lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials] makes $h=(t_1,\ldots,t_r,g_1,\ldots,g_s):V\to\mathbf A^{r+s}_F$ etale after shrinking. The projection $\mathbf A^{r+s}_F\to\mathbf A^r_F$ is the affine $s$-space projection over $\mathbf A^r_F$, so it is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth]. Etale maps are smooth by [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Their composite $c=(t_i)$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition].

source.place: Tags 06AA, lemma-differentials-relative-immersion-smooth; 02GU, lemma-etale-at-point; 01VA, lemma-composition-smooth; coordinate-basis extension as in more-morphisms.tex Tag 0FUE, lemma-etale-local-structure

proof.text: On the resulting neighbourhood construct $L$ from the prelog chart $\mathbf N^r\to\mathcal O$, $e_i\mapsto t_i$, using [lem-trf-associated-log-universal-stalks]. Its characteristic at a point is $\mathbf N^s$ for the vanishing coordinates, and its triviality locus is $D(\prod t_i)=X\setminus B$ on this neighbourhood. The $0\to\mathbf N^r$ comparison is the smooth map of Step 9, so [lem-trf-log-smooth-log-regular] applies over the trivial log field. In addition to log regularity, its statement canonically identifies $L$ with $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O_U^\times$, which is precisely the specified $M$. Thus $\mathbf N^r$ is a chart for $M$. Steps 4--5 show that $V(\prod t_i)$ is reduced; its support is the union of the chosen component supports, namely $B$ here. By uniqueness of the reduced induced closed subscheme it equals $D$ on this neighbourhood. We have proved (b), and Step 6 gives (a).

source.place: VI 1.4 and 1.8, pp.69--70; relative smooth-pair conclusion in X Lemma 2.2 proof, p.149

proof.text: If $r=0$, all products are $1$, all intersections with the empty index set are $V$, the characteristic is zero, and the comparison is the smooth structural map to $\mathbf A^0_F=\operatorname{Spec}F$. This handles $B=\varnothing$ and points outside the boundary. Nothing chooses global labels for branches, so distinct local branches may belong to one global component. All field-dependent inputs above assume only that $F$ is a field and use actual smoothness of the intersections, so the argument applies unchanged to imperfect fields.
